title: HARDEV CONSTRUCTION PRIVATE LIMITED VS. UNION OF INDIA

paras.text:
2026 INSC 1110
CA@ SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026 Page 1 of 7
Non-Reportable
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO. OF 2026
(Arising out of SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026)
Hardev Construction Private Limited
 ...Appellant(s)
Versus
Union of India & Ors.
...Respondent(s)
J U D G M E N T
K.VINOD CHANDRAN, J.
Leave granted.
2. The appellant's bid for the project 'Engineering
Procurement and Construction (EPC) of Construction of guide
bunds, Launching Aprons and Associated River Protection
Works etc. in connection with Bikramshila-Katareah New Line
Rail Link Project on EPC Mode"-Bid/ Package No. ECR-CAO-C-S-EPC-05-25-26 dated 06.01.2026' was rejected for reason of
non-submission of original of the Bid Security furnished;
stipulated vide Clause 2.20.6 (ii) of the Request For Proposal
(RFP), as indicated in the e-portal of the respondent, a copy

CA@ SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026 Page 2 of 7
of which is produced at Annexure P3. The Division Bench of
the Patna High Court affirmed the rejection, which is
impugned in the instant appeal.
3. We heard Sri A. K. De, learned Counsel for the
appellant, Sri Kanakamedala Ravindra Kumar, learned A.S.G.
for the respondent-Ministry of Railways and Ms. Nina R.
Nariman, learned Counsel for the 3rd respondent, who was
the successful tenderer.
4. Learned Counsel for the appellant points out that the
rejection was only on the ground that the appellant had not
submitted the original of the Bid Security furnished, which in
the case of the appellant was submitted through the e-payment Gateway of Authority. The Bid Security was remitted
to the account of the respondent through e-payment, the
receipt of which in the digital form was scanned and
uploaded along with the bid.
5. Learned A.S.G. for the respondent-Ministry of
Railways, however, points out that Clause 2.20.6(ii)
specifically requires the original to be submitted, and in that
circumstance, the rejection was proper. Learned Counsel for
the 3rd respondent relied on the decision in Prakash

CA@ SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026 Page 3 of 7
Asphaltings and Toll Highways (India) Ltd. v. Mandeepa
Enterprises and Others1 to argue that the awarder is the best
equipped to understand and appreciate its requirements and
interpret bid documents and the Constitutional Courts should
defer to such understanding and appreciation of the tender
documents. There is no elbow room insofar as producing the
original documents, is the 3
rd respondent's contention.
6. Learned Counsel for the appellant also points out that
his financial bid was far lower than that of the 3rd respondent
and this causes loss to the exchequer. Learned A.S.G. alertly
points out that there was no opportunity to compare the
financial bids, since the appellant had failed in its technical
bid at the inception, for non-production of the required
original receipt, and in that circumstance, the appellant's
financial bid was never opened.
7. Clause 2.20.6 of the RFP, produced as Annexure P1,
speaks of submission of Bid Security in the form of Bank
Guarantee/ Account Payee Demand Draft/Fixed Deposit
Receipt/ Banker's Cheque/ e-payment Gateway of Authority.
It is also stipulated in Clause 1 that a scanned copy of the
1
(2026) 4 SCC 310

CA@ SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026 Page 4 of 7
same shall be uploaded on e-Procurement Portal while
applying for the tender. There is no dispute that the appellant
made payment of the Bid Security by means of e-payment
and the rejection was only on the ground of violation of
Clause (ii). Clause (ii) prescribes that the form in which the
Bid Security is furnished, should be delivered in person,
physically, to the official nominated, as indicated in the
tender document. The appellant's contention is that there is
no question of production of an original, since the payment
has already gone into the coffers of the respondents and the
digital receipt has been uploaded along with the tender
document.
8. We are perfectly in agreement with the contention of
the appellant, especially looking at the various forms in
which the Bid Security can be furnished; a Bank Guarantee/
Account Payee Demand Draft/Fixed Deposit Receipt/
Banker's Cheque, unless physically furnished to the
respondent, there can be no lien exercised on the Bid
Security. It is, hence, the stipulation that at the time of
application, the scanned copy should be uploaded and later
the original should be handed over to the nominated official.

CA@ SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026 Page 5 of 7
Insofar as the appellant is concerned, the money was
deposited to the account of the respondents and there is
nothing further required to be produced insofar as the e-payment made, especially when the digital payment receipt
had been uploaded along with the bid document.
9. Prakash Asphaltings and Toll Highways (India) Ltd.1
was a case in which a tender was invited for toll collection.
When the financial bid was opened, tenderers whose
technical bid was found to be qualified; three of them, had
quoted in crores while one had quoted a paltry amount of
Rs.9,72,999/-. The contention raised was that this was a bona
fide mistake, and the financial bid indicated only the
collection of a single day and if it is worked out for the total
contract of 1095 days, it would be Rs.100.65 crores and then
their bid would be the highest. It was in this context that this
Court held that the words used in the tender documents
cannot be ignored or treated as redundant or superfluous.
The tenderer was required to give the total collection for the
contract period and an omission insofar as submitting a paltry
amount, even if inadvertent, cannot be explained by putting
forth the contention that the bid was mistakenly quoted at the

CA@ SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026 Page 6 of 7
per day rate. It is also pertinent that this Court in the aforesaid
decision, while cautioning the Constitutional Court's to defer
to the understanding and appreciation of the tender
documents, also carved out an exception insofar as mala fide
and perverse understanding or appreciation of the
documents, especially in the application of the terms of the
tender document.
10. We are convinced that here, there is a clear
perversity; insofar as an e-payment was made, as required
by the tender document, the digital receipt of which was
scanned and uploaded, rejected only since the original was
not produced; which is an impossibility. Rigid adherence to
the letter of a document cannot be countenanced, especially
when there is a clear impossibility in compliance of the same.
As we noticed, Bid Security, when furnished in all other
forms, cannot be enforced, unless the original comes into the
hands of the respondents. However, insofar as the e-payment
is concerned, the money has already been transferred to the
account of the respondents, and they have full control over it.
11. We, hence, set aside the impugned order and direct
the contract to be awarded to the appellant herein.

CA@ SLP (C) No.25855 of 2026 Page 7 of 7
12. We have been informed by the learned Counsel for
the appellant that after rejection, the amounts deposited in
the e-portal was refunded to the appellant. In that
circumstance, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 would facilitate
either a measure of e-payment within a period of two weeks
from today, and if there is any technical difficulty, then the
appellant shall be required to submit the amounts in any
other form within a further period of two weeks. On the
submission of the Bid Security, the appellant's financial bid
shall be opened to be considered along with the other bids
and the tender finalized, in accordance with the other tender
conditions stipulated.
13. The appeal stands allowed with the above directions.
14. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand rejected.

NEW DELHI;
